features.name: Pipeline and case workflow orchestration
features.summary: Lets teams define multi-stage pipelines with configurable, optionally-enforced stage transitions, then drive work through them as cases: ingest (single or batch), list/search by stage/parent/terminal state, claim/release with expiring leases, and transition with optimistic version checks. Cases support AI-style stage-transition suggestions (with rationale and confidence) that reviewers accept or dismiss, a review inbox with approve/reject/request-changes and bulk review from file, cross-case blocking relationships, parent/child hierarchies, and per-stage on-enter automations that run routines.

features.name: Isolated instance lifecycle: background service, seeded worktrees, and managed secrets
features.summary: Runs the platform as a supervised local service (install/start/stop/restart with health polling and a lock-protected hot-restart handshake that writes intent/report files and waits for a specific server version). Provides isolated git-worktree instances seeded from another instance's database — backup/restore, migrations, rebound workspaces — while quarantining execution (disabling timer heartbeats, resetting running agents, quarantining in-progress issues) and later merging issue/comment/attachment/document history back. Also manages a .env file next to the config, generating and persisting the agent JWT secret and atomically merging only PAPERCLIP_-owned entries.

features.name: Self-updating managed CLI installs with rollback
features.summary: Maintains a versioned install store under the Paperclip home directory holding multiple CLI payloads from npm or git sources across channels (latest, canary, pinned), tracked by a manifest that records previous versions for rollback. Activation is an atomic flip of a `current` symlink guarded by marker/ownership/symlink safety checks and a PID-aware cross-process lock, with a shim binary in ~/.local/bin and a managed PATH block in shell configs.

features.name: Cross-platform background service supervision
features.summary: Registers and controls the platform as a native user service on Linux (systemd) and macOS (launchd) by rendering escaped unit/plist definitions and writing them atomically with ownership and symlink-safety checks. Supports install/uninstall, start/stop/restart, status with reported PID, log following, start-on-login enablement, and systemd linger (with explicit consent) so the service runs without an active login session.

files.summary: Registers the `pipelines` CLI command group covering pipeline CRUD (create/list/get), transition-edge replacement, guidance documents, per-stage `run_routine` on-enter automations, case ingest (single and batch from file), case listing/editing, lease-based claim/release, version-checked transitions, transition suggestions with accept/dismiss resolution, a review flow (approve/reject/request-changes with edits), blocking relationships, and a review inbox with bulk review. All commands resolve company context and call REST endpoints under /api/companies/:id/pipelines and /api/pipelines/:id, printing as formatted text or JSON.
behavior: Creates pipelines with stages supplied inline (--stages-json) or from a file, and can replace the full transition edge set and toggle transition enforcement via set-transitions.
Case operations are concurrency-safe by design: claim/release take lease tokens, and transitions/reviews/edits require an expectedVersion plus optional leaseToken.
Exposes a suggestion workflow (suggest with rationale/confidence, then resolve-suggestion with accept/dismiss) and a review inbox supporting bulk decisions loaded from a JSON file.

files.summary: Implements the `service` CLI group for managing Paperclip as a background service (install with optional linger consent, uninstall, start/stop/restart, status/logs) and a hot-restart flow used by the platform itself. Hot restart is serialized by a PID-aware file lock, writes a hot-restart-intent.json (previous PID/version, drain flag, requesting run ID), triggers the service manager restart, polls the local health endpoint until the expected server version appears, and reads back a hot-restart-report.json.
behavior: Probes a local health URL with a 2s timeout and polls it up to 60s until the reported serverVersion matches an expected version after restart.
Acquires an exclusive hot-restart.lock per instance, stealing the lock only when the owning PID is dead, so concurrent restarts cannot interleave.
Install prompts for explicit consent before enabling systemd linger so the service can run without an active login session.

files.summary: Implements worktree commands that create isolated Paperclip instances as git worktrees (init/make/list/env, reseed, repair, ensure-seeded, merge-history). Seeding copies another instance's state by backing up and restoring Postgres (including an embedded Postgres runtime), applying pending migrations, rebounding workspace paths, and quarantining execution — disabling timer heartbeats, resetting running agents, quarantining in-progress issues, unassigning todo/review issues, and stopping workspace/runtime services. merge-history plans and applies issue, comment, attachment, and document changes back from the worktree with dry-run support.
behavior: Names are normalized to a `paperclip-` prefix and validated against [A-Za-z0-9._-]; worktree home and start point resolve from flags or PAPERCLIP_* env vars.

Seed results report a structured quarantine summary (disabled heartbeats, reset agents, quarantined issues, stopped runtimes) plus validation counts (auth users, companies, issues, migration revision).
Object storage keys are normalized and path-checked (no `..`, company-prefixed, path-containment assert) before any local or S3 read/write.

files.summary: Manages the .env file located next to the resolved config path: lazy-loads it once per process (dotenv, no override), filters writes to Paperclip-owned keys matching /^PAPERCLIP_[A-Z0-9_]+$/, and updates the file atomically only when contents change. It also ensures an agent JWT secret exists under PAPERCLIP_AGENT_JWT_SECRET, generating a 32-byte hex value and persisting it on first use.
behavior: Reads PAPERCLIP_AGENT_JWT_SECRET from the environment first, falling back to the .env file, and creates a random 32-byte hex secret only when neither exists.
Writes only touch PAPERCLIP_-prefixed non-empty entries, leaving user-owned variables in the same .env file untouched.
Each env file is loaded at most once per process via a loadedEnvFiles set, with dotenv configured not to override existing environment variables.

files.summary: Implements the managed CLI install store under the Paperclip home: versioned payloads from npm or git across latest/canary/pinned channels, an install.json manifest recording the active record plus previous installs for rollback, a managed-store marker, and a PID-aware exclusive lock for install operations. Activation flips a `current` symlink atomically after validating that the payload directory is a real, owned directory inside the installs root; a shim path and shell PATH block markers are also defined here.
behavior: Refuses to operate on install-store paths that are symlinks, not owned by the current user, multi-linked, or missing the exact managed-store marker string.
Acquires the install lock via write-temp-then-link; steals the lock only when the recorded owner PID is no longer alive, and errors name the stale lock path.
Manifest writes and current-symlink flips are atomic (temp file + rename), and payloads must resolve inside the installs root before activation.

files.summary: Defines the ServiceManager interface and its systemd and launchd implementations, which render escaped unit files / plists and drive them through systemctl --user or launchctl. Install writes the definition only if changed (with daemon-reload on change), enables/disables start-on-login, optionally enables linger, and uninstall stops, disables, removes the definition, and resets failed state; status parses LoadState/ActiveState/UnitFileState/MainPID (or launchd equivalents) into a normalized ServiceStatus.
behavior: Systemd values are escaped (backslashes, quotes, $, %) and plist values XML-escaped, with line breaks rejected in systemd values.
Service definitions are written atomically through temp-file+rename and only into directories owned by the current user, refusing symlinked or foreign-owned targets.
Both managers keep the service alive by default: Restart=always with 5s delay (systemd) and KeepAlive with RunAtLoad (launchd), with 300s stop timeouts.
